### 🔁 The room keeps playing after a match
- When a PvP match ends, the end screen offers a ballot of maps and a short clock. When it runs out, the room loads the winner and lands on it in warmup — nobody has to go back to the menu.
- **Every game mode is on the ballot**, not just the ones the offered maps happen to support. The room votes for a mode and the map that can host it wins; the tiles are picked so that a vote for CTF or Hardpoint always has somewhere to land.
- **The map you just played is always offered.** "This ground again, a different game" is the most ordinary thing a room wants after a good match.
- The vote covers the settings too: economy, match length, time of day and weather. Anything nobody voted on stays the way the room already had it.
- You can see who voted for what, and change your vote while the clock runs. The host starts the next match when everyone has landed, so there is a moment to look around the new map first.
- Late arrivals can join again at the end screen instead of waiting out the whole session — they walk into the vote and are playing a minute later.

### 📐 Editors snap to a grid
- Moving, resizing and rotating in the map and structure editor now snaps to a grid, so walls actually meet in game instead of only looking aligned from the editor camera.
- The grid step (and a separate rotation step) is picked in the toolbar and remembered between sessions, with the lattice drawn under whatever you are working on.
- `Round` tidies a whole map at once — useful for anything authored before the grid existed or dropped in by a preset.
- New **Underground** storey: cellars and tunnels dug into terrain sculpted below the ground plane, with its own eye toggle like every other floor.

### 🔥 A torch for your walls
- A wall sconce with a real burning torch in it — the flame flickers and the light on the floor breathes with it. It burns the same fire as the torch in your hand.

### 🏆 Arms Race goes the distance
- The ladder is now every weapon in the game bar the survival tools: fifteen rungs, with the flamethrower, the launcher, the Scout and the bow slotted in where their difficulty puts them.
- Dying hands you back exactly the rung you are on — no hoarded medkits carried into the next match, and the single-shot weapons come with enough ammunition to actually clear their rung.

### ✨ The menus look like the game again
- The map preview behind the main menu and the lobby now draws maps through the game's own lighting, fog, grass and outlines. What you see before a match is what the match looks like.
- The end screen is one tidy column instead of a narrow scoreboard inside a full-width frame, and it scrolls on small windows.
- Aiming is smoother in the desktop app: the mouse is polled ~3× more often, which removes a per-frame wobble at constant hand speed.

### 🧹 Removed
- The **Arcade movement** setting (sliding, air-strafing, bunny hopping) is gone. One movement feel, the shipped one.
